summary: NASA is adopting Apollo-era urgency as it advances its Artemis program, aiming to establish a moon base and land astronauts on the lunar surface within two years. In scientific developments, new research indicates the Milky Way’s disk grew "upside down," with younger stars forming in ever-thinner layers over time. Cosmologists have also deployed the record-breaking Lumina simulation to map dark matter and replicate the early universe on an unprecedented scale, while solar physics research shows that flare ribbons can reveal previously hidden explosions on the sun. For observational astronomy, tonight brings seasonal celestial targets including potential fireballs alongside October's "Hunter's Moon." Looking ahead, readers should keep an eye on the evening sky tonight to watch the October "Hunter's Moon" rise into the autumn sky.
